evals.name: discover-scattered-checkout-policy
evals.prompt: Review the checkout area of this codebase before we add partial refunds. Recent changes keep touching controllers, Stripe wrappers, and order models. Find the architectural friction and help me choose a safe seam for an implementation agent.
evals.expected_output: A change-pressure diagnosis, knowledge/change/policy map, no more than three earned candidates, and a human selection gate. The run stops before designing an interface or contract because the user has not selected a candidate.

evals.name: design-selected-refund-module
evals.prompt: From the architecture review, I choose the candidate that localizes refund policy in the Order domain. Design that module twice so I can choose the interface. Do not implement it.
evals.expected_output: At least two materially different coarse interfaces compared on caller load, information hiding, change containment, dependency direction, current usefulness, and testability, followed by a human design-selection gate. No contract is finalized before the user chooses.

evals.name: contract-approved-refund-design
evals.prompt: I choose the second refund-policy interface. Turn that approved architecture into the fence that spec and implementation should carry forward.
evals.expected_output: A named architecture contract for one neighborhood with authorized behavior, ownership, interface guarantees, allowed neighborhood, predicted touchpoints, dependency and boundary-data rules, hard guards versus diagnostic signals, escalation conditions, and checkpoint cadence.

evals.name: architecture-checkpoint
evals.prompt: Run an architecture checkpoint on planning task 1042 using its approved password-reset contract and exact batch patch /tmp/reset-1042.patch with digest abc123. Tell me whether the next two related stories can run autonomously.
evals.expected_output: A contract-to-isolated-patch comparison covering behavior, predicted and actual touchpoints, knowledge ownership, dependency direction, boundary data, and hard guards; one explicit Continue/Reorganize first/Human decision gate; a human acceptance gate; and instructions to persist the accepted result on the planning task.

evals.name: no-unearned-refactor
evals.prompt: Our repository has a 700-line parser that changes about once every two years. Can you improve the architecture and split it into cleaner modules for agents?
evals.expected_output: The skill weighs actual change frequency and complexity before proposing structure, resists size-driven splitting, and may conclude that no refactor is earned unless representative changes reveal amplification, cognitive load, or hidden obligations.

assertions: Diagnoses change amplification, cognitive load, and unknown unknowns before proposing structure
Maps knowledge ownership, change ownership, and policy versus replaceable detail
Does not use file or function size alone as an architecture finding
Keeps candidate and interface choices behind explicit human gates
Compares at least two coarse interface designs only after a candidate is selected
Produces an architecture contract containing ownership, dependency direction, scope, verification, escalation, and checkpoint cadence
Separates hard deterministic guards from diagnostic quality signals
Checkpoint mode requires an isolated batch and returns exactly one Continue, Reorganize first, or Human decision gate
Accepted checkpoint gates and contract revisions are persisted in K2412/planning
